paragraphs: Recognizing someone's intention from multiple kinds of input requires deciding how much to trust each source. Those sources can differ in usefulness, reliability, and noise. A model may become overly dependent on the strongest modality and underuse others, making its predictions less dependable when the dominant source deteriorates. This paper treats that imbalance as a problem occurring at more than one level.

Adaptive Re-calibration Learning addresses individual examples and the model's broader structure together. Its sample-level mechanism dynamically masks modalities that contribute too strongly, encouraging the model to learn from neglected inputs. Its structural mechanism adjusts encoder weights according to each modality's overall contribution. The two mechanisms therefore influence both what information the model encounters during learning and how its encoders are weighted.

Across multiple intention-recognition benchmarks, the authors report significant improvements in accuracy and robustness over existing methods. The gains are especially apparent when inputs are noisy or modalities are degraded. These results support addressing sample-specific dominance alongside broader encoder imbalance when training multimodal intention-recognition systems.
neurips-2025-adaptive-re-calibration-lea.tldr: ARL balances multimodal intention recognition through sample masking and encoder reweighting, improving reported accuracy and robustness.

paragraphs: Teaching a robot through human corrections involves two connected problems: collecting useful interventions while the robot acts, and turning those interventions into better behavior. These problems become especially important in precise manipulation involving physical contact. Compliant Residual DAgger addresses both the correction interface and the policy that learns from the resulting data.

The interface uses compliance control so that people can supply gentle, precise changes to the robot's actions without stopping its ongoing policy execution. These are delta corrections: adjustments to what the robot is already doing. A residual policy then learns from those corrections while incorporating force feedback and force control. This connects the human's adjustments with the physical forces encountered during manipulation.

In real-world book-flipping and belt-assembly tasks, the authors report improvements of over 60% in base-policy success rates using minimal correction data. The system also outperforms retraining from scratch and fine-tuning in their experiments. The findings show how coordinated choices about intervention collection and policy updates can make human corrections useful for demanding contact tasks.
neurips-2025-compliant-residual-dagger-i.tldr: CR-DAgger combines gentle human interventions with force-aware residual learning to improve precise robot manipulation using little correction data.

paragraphs: Chip floorplanning determines an initial layout that affects later placement, routing, and power. Its enormous search space makes it difficult for an optimizer to explore enough alternatives, and a search can settle on a locally attractive solution. CORE combines evolutionary search with reinforcement learning to improve exploration and layout quality.

The evolutionary component directly modifies layouts and develops a population using both novelty and performance. Clustering supports diversity within that search. The reinforcement-learning component treats floorplanning as a sequence of decisions using a B*-Tree representation. Two coordination mechanisms connect them: reinforcement learning helps accelerate population evolution, while the evolutionary search provides guidance for the learner. Each component therefore contributes to the other's optimization process.

On the MCNC and GSRC benchmarks, CORE outperforms strong comparison methods on wirelength and area utilization, with a reported 12.9% improvement in wirelength. The authors also report that it surpasses existing reinforcement-learning approaches. These findings support combining population diversity with learned sequential decisions for the evaluated floorplanning problems.
neurips-2025-core-collaborative-optimiza.tldr: CORE coordinates evolutionary search and reinforcement learning to improve chip floorplans, reporting a 12.9% wirelength improvement.

paragraphs: Scientific datasets can contain a few common categories and extremely scarce categories that carry substantial scientific interest. The setting studied here combines severe imbalance with relatively few classes and limited total data. Methods developed for more conventional long-tailed benchmarks can favor majority classes or overfit the few rare examples, undermining recognition of the cases researchers most want to find.

The proposed framework joins two mechanisms. Balanced Supervised Contrastive Learning dynamically reweights class contributions to strengthen representations of rare categories. Smooth Objective Regularization manages the tension between emphasizing those categories and maintaining overall classification performance. The authors also introduce the ZincFluor chemical dataset and use CIFAR-LT variants with controllable imbalance to examine this setting.

The method achieves 66.84% Tail Top-2 accuracy on ZincFluor. On CIFAR-10-LT with an imbalance ratio of 1000, it reaches 38.99% tail-class accuracy, substantially exceeding the next-best method in the reported evaluation. These results demonstrate improved rare-class recognition on the tested datasets and suggest potential value for scientific discovery under extreme imbalance.
neurips-2025-deciphering-the-extremes-a-.tldr: Balanced contrastive learning and smooth regularization improve rare-class recognition in small scientific datasets with extreme imbalance.

paragraphs: Classifying an entire graph requires combining its node representations into a graph-level summary. This pooling step can influence how vulnerable the final prediction is to adversarial changes. While many defenses concentrate on message passing between nodes, this paper examines pooling itself as a source of vulnerability and an opportunity for stronger defenses.

The authors derive upper bounds on adversarial risk for sum, average, and maximum pooling, identifying weaknesses associated with different attacks and graph structures. Their proposed Robust Singular Pooling constructs a graph representation using the dominant singular vector of the node-embedding matrix. They analyze its robustness theoretically and explain the resulting bound. Power iteration provides an efficient way to implement the operation.

The theoretical analysis focuses on Graph Convolutional Networks, although the pooling method can be used with other models. On real-world benchmarks under the evaluated adversarial attacks, it provides better robustness than the pooling alternatives considered while retaining competitive accuracy on unmodified data. The contribution makes graph summarization an explicit part of robustness design.
neurips-2025-enhancing-graph-classificat.tldr: Robust Singular Pooling improves evaluated graph-classification robustness by building graph summaries from the dominant singular vector of node embeddings.

paragraphs: A robot intended for general-purpose manipulation needs to perform tasks beyond those represented in its training. This paper examines that ability in vision-language-action models through AGNOSTOS, a simulation benchmark with 23 unseen manipulation tasks. The tasks differ from common training distributions, and two difficulty levels allow the evaluation to probe different degrees of generalization.

The authors find that existing models struggle on these tasks despite their diverse training data. They propose Cross-Task In-Context Manipulation, which supplies a language model with demonstrations from previously seen tasks and asks it to predict action sequences for unseen ones. A dynamics-guided selection strategy chooses relevant demonstrations by considering relationships in task dynamics.

On AGNOSTOS, the proposed method improves cross-task zero-shot generalization, with reported gains of 6.0% over π₀ and 7.9% over VoxPoser. Here, unseen-task prediction still uses demonstrations from seen tasks as context. The results suggest that selecting and reusing relevant experience can help with the transfer difficulties exposed by this simulation benchmark.
neurips-2025-exploring-the-limits-of-vis.tldr: AGNOSTOS exposes unseen-task weaknesses in robot models, while dynamics-guided demonstrations improve cross-task action prediction.

paragraphs: Contextual bandit algorithms must balance trying uncertain actions with choosing actions that appear rewarding. Feel-Good Thompson Sampling adds an optimism bonus to ordinary Thompson Sampling, favoring models that predict higher rewards. Its theoretical appeal includes asymptotically minimax-optimal regret in the linear setting with exact posteriors. This paper asks how its practical behavior changes when posterior sampling is approximate.

The authors evaluate the method and a smoothed variant across fourteen synthetic and real-world benchmarks. They compare exact-posterior settings with approximations generated by fast stochastic-gradient samplers. Additional experiments vary preconditioning, the optimism bonus, and prior strength. These choices help separate the influence of optimism from the accuracy of the samples used to implement it.

Larger bonuses help when posterior samples are accurate but can hurt when sampling noise dominates. Feel-Good Thompson Sampling generally beats ordinary Thompson Sampling in linear and logistic bandits, yet tends to perform worse in neural bandits. The authors recommend the variants as accessible, competitive baselines, while their findings make sampling quality central to interpreting their performance.
neurips-2025-feel-good-thompson-sampling.tldr: Feel-Good Thompson Sampling often helps with accurate posterior samples, but stronger optimism can hurt when approximate sampling is noisy.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning can teach a language model facts that support useful new deductions, but it can also produce incorrect claims. This paper argues that both outcomes can arise from out-of-context reasoning: associating concepts to infer implications, including when those concepts lack a causal connection. Experiments across five language models support this account, with the outcome depending on whether the associations are causal.

To investigate the mechanism, the authors formulate a synthetic factual-recall task. A one-layer, single-head, attention-only transformer learns the task when its output and value matrices are factorized. A model using combined weights does not in their experiments. This isolates matrix factorization as an important feature of the studied setup.

The theoretical analysis connects the behavior to gradient descent's preference for solutions with a smaller nuclear norm of the combined output-value matrix. That structure explains efficient learning of associations without distinguishing causal relationships from spurious correlations. The theory provides a mechanism for the simplified task and a perspective on why injecting knowledge can support both generalization and hallucination.
neurips-2025-generalization-or-hallucina.tldr: The paper links useful generalization and hallucination to a shared association mechanism, with a theoretical explanation in a simplified transformer.

paragraphs: Biological sequence design seeks sequences that meet desired functional objectives. Discrete diffusion models offer a way to generate them, and reinforcement-learning-based tuning can help adapt generation when data are limited or several objectives matter. The paper identifies a practical tension: existing gradient-free approaches can be unstable in discrete optimization, while gradient-based approaches can require substantial computation.

GLID²E is a gradient-free reinforcement-learning approach for tuning discrete diffusion models. It combines a clipped likelihood constraint, which regulates the exploration space, with reward shaping, which brings generation into closer alignment with design goals. Together, these mechanisms address how broadly the method explores and how it evaluates progress toward the desired sequence properties.

The authors report that the combination mitigates instabilities encountered in reinforcement learning and diffusion-based tuning. Evaluations in DNA and protein sequence design show competitive performance for function-based objectives while maintaining computational efficiency and flexible tuning. The contribution is a way to balance control, stability, and computational demands in the evaluated biological design systems.
neurips-2025-glid-2-e-a-gradient-free-li.tldr: GLID²E uses constrained exploration and reward shaping for stable, efficient gradient-free tuning of biological sequence diffusion models.

paragraphs: Imagine360 turns an ordinary perspective video into a full 360-degree video, using the original footage as an anchor. The goal is to generate a surrounding dynamic scene that viewers can explore in every direction. This requires learning both spherical visual structure and motion patterns from limited panoramic video data.

The system uses separate perspective and panorama denoising branches to provide local and global constraints. Motion modules and spatial LoRA layers are fine-tuned on 360-degree videos. An antipodal mask addresses long-range motion relationships between opposite parts of the sphere, including reversed camera motion across hemispheres. Rotation-aware components also accommodate changing camera poses, which alter the masked regions associated with the input video.

The authors introduce a dataset of 10,000 trimmed 360-degree clips with structured motion to support training. Their experiments report better visual quality and motion coherence than the compared state-of-the-art methods when using the curated dataset. The findings support adapting generation to spherical geometry and camera motion as part of making personalized panoramic video creation more accessible.
neurips-2025-imagine360-immersive-360-vi.tldr: Imagine360 expands perspective videos into panoramic videos using local and global generation constraints plus spherical motion modeling.

paragraphs: Incomplete knowledge can require uncertainty representations richer than a single probability distribution. Imprecise probability models represent ambiguity and partial belief, but their variety creates a challenge: how should differences between such models be measured? This paper develops a common mathematical framework for comparing them and quantifying the uncertainty they express.

Integral Imprecise Probability Metrics extend classical integral probability metrics through the Choquet integral to capacities, a broad family that includes probability intervals, lower probabilities, and belief functions. The authors establish conditions under which the construction is a valid metric and captures a form of weak convergence. These are conditional mathematical results about when the proposed comparison behaves appropriately.

Comparing an imprecise model with its conjugate produces Maximum Mean Imprecision, a new family of epistemic-uncertainty measures satisfying key proposed axioms. In selective-classification experiments, these measures perform strongly against established alternatives and outperform them when classical methods struggle with large numbers of classes. The framework therefore connects formal comparison of uncertainty models with a practical way to measure incomplete knowledge within one model.
neurips-2025-integral-imprecise-probabil.tldr: A new metric framework compares imprecise probability models and yields uncertainty measures with strong selective-classification results.

paragraphs: Using several language models together has inspired many systems described as multi-agent. This position paper argues that much of that work adopts the terminology without engaging sufficiently with the ideas developed in multi-agent systems research. Its central concern is whether these implementations meaningfully embody agency, social interaction, and structured environments.

The authors organize their analysis around four areas: the social dimension of agency, environment design, coordination and communication protocols, and the measurement of emergent behavior. They argue that many current implementations use oversimplified architectures centered on language models and lack important multi-agent characteristics. This framing asks researchers to examine how components interact and act within an environment, beyond simply counting participating models.

The paper warns that overlooking existing multi-agent research could slow progress by revisiting problems that literature has already addressed. It outlines research opportunities and advocates closer integration of established concepts alongside more precise terminology. As a position paper, its contribution is a conceptual critique and research direction, rather than a reported performance improvement from a new system.
neurips-2025-large-language-models-miss-.tldr: This position paper argues that many multi-LLM systems overlook foundational multi-agent concepts, limiting both clarity and research opportunities.

paragraphs: Reasoning models often produce intermediate thinking drafts before their final answers, potentially exploring several reasoning paths. For those drafts to support monitoring and interpretation, their contents need to meaningfully influence the model's subsequent reasoning and response. This paper evaluates that relationship through deliberate counterfactual changes to the draft.

The framework separates two questions. Intra-draft faithfulness asks whether individual steps causally affect later steps and the draft's conclusion; the authors test this by inserting counterfactual reasoning steps. Draft-to-answer faithfulness asks whether the final answer depends on, and is logically consistent with, the draft. To test that relationship, they perturb the logic at the draft's conclusion.

Experiments across six leading reasoning models find selective responsiveness to intermediate steps and frequent failures to align final answers with draft conclusions. These findings distinguish the presence of an elaborate reasoning trace from evidence that its stated steps guide the outcome. They motivate more faithful reasoning processes if thinking drafts are to provide reliable tools for interpretation, monitoring, and control.
neurips-2025-measuring-the-faithfulness-.tldr: Counterfactual interventions reveal selective faithfulness within reasoning drafts and frequent mismatches between draft conclusions and final answers.

paragraphs: Sign-language models need features that capture relationships relevant to signing, beyond visual contours and textures. Graph-based approaches can connect regions within a frame and across time, but the paper highlights a tradeoff: strengthening those cross-region relationships may weaken the representations of individual regions. MixSignGraph is designed to preserve useful local detail alongside those broader connections.

The model combines local and temporal sign graphs with a hierarchical sign graph. After cross-region features are extracted, the hierarchical component gathers features for the same region from frame representations at different levels of granularity. This strengthens discriminative local information. For gloss-free tasks, the authors also introduce text-based CTC pretraining, generating pseudo gloss labels from text sequences to provide pretraining supervision.

Experiments span five sign-language datasets and multiple tasks. The authors report that MixSignGraph exceeds most current models across several datasets without additional cues. The results support combining cross-region modeling with explicit restoration of local representations, while the text-derived pretraining offers an additional route to improving gloss-free performance.
neurips-2025-mixsigngraph-a-sign-sequenc.tldr: MixSignGraph combines spatial, temporal, and hierarchical graphs to strengthen sign-language features, with text-derived pretraining for gloss-free tasks.

paragraphs: Cellular datasets often provide snapshots at a few times, leaving researchers to infer the processes connecting them. Those processes include changes in cell state, proliferation, and communication between cells. The paper argues that existing transport and Schrödinger-bridge approaches have limited ability to account for interactions, even though those interactions can influence how cells change state.

The authors formulate the Unbalanced Mean-Field Schrödinger Bridge to describe stochastic dynamics with both population changes and interactions. They then introduce CytoBridge, a deep-learning algorithm that approximates this framework. Neural networks explicitly model cellular transitions, proliferation, and interactions, allowing these connected processes to be learned directly from snapshot data.

Evaluation uses synthetic gene-regulatory data and real single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. Compared with existing methods, CytoBridge identifies growth, transition, and interaction patterns, removes false transitions, and reconstructs developmental landscapes more accurately in the reported experiments. The contribution brings interactions into the same modeling framework as cell-state changes and growth, improving reconstruction of the cellular dynamics examined.
neurips-2025-modeling-cell-dynamics-and-.tldr: CytoBridge jointly models cell transitions, proliferation, and interactions from sparse snapshots, improving reported developmental reconstructions.

paragraphs: Computer-use agents can automate tasks through vision-language models, but key details of highly capable systems often remain closed. OpenCUA addresses the research community's need to inspect and develop these systems by providing an open framework covering demonstration collection, training data, processing infrastructure, and agent models.

An annotation tool captures human computer-use demonstrations. The resulting AgentNet dataset spans three operating systems and more than 200 applications and websites. A scalable processing pipeline turns demonstrations into state-action pairs accompanied by reflective, extended reasoning. The authors report that this pipeline sustains performance gains as the amount of data increases, connecting the collection infrastructure with scalable model training.

OpenCUA-72B achieves an average success rate of 45.0% on OSWorld-Verified, which the authors report as a new best result among open-source models. Further analysis finds good cross-domain generalization and substantial benefits from additional computation at test time. Releasing the tools, data, code, and models provides a concrete foundation for studying computer-use capabilities, limitations, and risks.
neurips-2025-opencua-open-foundations-fo.tldr: OpenCUA releases a full computer-use-agent framework, with its 72B model achieving 45.0% average success on OSWorld-Verified.

paragraphs: Recourse explanations tell people rejected by an algorithm what they could change to receive a positive decision. This paper examines a feedback problem: when many people follow that advice, their collective actions can alter the data used to retrain the decision model. The resulting decision boundary may move, leaving people rejected again despite having made the recommended changes.

The authors formally characterize conditions under which recourse remains valid after these effects occur. Their analysis shows that recommendations may become invalid when they depend on non-causal variables or instruct people to change them. The concern therefore involves both the information used to choose an action and the variables the action directly changes.

Based on this analysis, the authors caution against standard counterfactual explanations and causal recourse methods, and advocate recommendations acting exclusively on causal variables. The result identifies a possible failure mechanism, rather than asserting that every recommendation involving a non-causal variable must fail. It makes the consequences of collective compliance and subsequent retraining central to evaluating whether recourse advice remains useful.
neurips-2025-performative-validity-of-re.tldr: Recourse advice can invalidate itself after collective behavior changes and model retraining, particularly when non-causal variables influence recommended actions.

paragraphs: Long intermediate reasoning can help language models solve difficult problems, but retaining the information associated with those lengthy traces consumes memory and slows token generation. Reasoning Path Compression targets that inference cost. It uses the observation that reasoning paths contain semantic sparsity: their stored information need not all receive equal importance during continued generation.

The method periodically compresses the key-value cache, keeping entries with high importance scores. Those scores are computed using a selector window of recently generated queries, so the selection reflects recent generation activity. RPC requires no model training. Its intervention concerns which cache entries remain available as reasoning proceeds, making cache management the central mechanism for improving efficiency.

For QwQ-32B, the experiments report generation throughput up to 1.60 times that of inference with a full cache, alongside a 1.2% accuracy drop on AIME 2024. This is an empirical speed–accuracy tradeoff. The finding supports using semantic sparsity to reduce the cost of long reasoning traces while retaining much of the evaluated model's accuracy.
neurips-2025-reasoning-path-compression-.tldr: RPC selectively compresses reasoning-model caches without training, reporting up to 1.60× throughput with a 1.2% accuracy drop.

paragraphs: One way to understand recurrent self-attention is to find an energy function that decreases as the state updates. However, such analyses often require symmetry, a single attention head, or other restrictions absent from more general architectures. This paper develops a dynamical-systems perspective that can study inference without requiring that kind of energy function.

The analysis centers on the state Jacobian, which describes sensitivity of an update to changes in the current state. It shows that normalization suppresses self-attention's Lipschitzness and the Jacobian's complex eigenvalues, associated with oscillatory dynamics. This provides a way to investigate stability and oscillation while relaxing constraints used in energy-based treatments.

Lyapunov exponents computed from the Jacobians indicate that normalized dynamics lie near a critical state. The authors find that this criticality is a strong indicator of high inference performance; the claim is an indicator relationship, rather than a universal performance guarantee. The same perspective supports training regularizers and a pseudo-energy for monitoring inference, linking the analysis to practical tools for examining recurrent attention.
neurips-2025-recurrent-self-attention-dy.tldr: Jacobian analysis explains aspects of recurrent self-attention dynamics without requiring an energy function and links near-critical behavior with strong inference performance.

paragraphs: Attempts to suppress toxic language often intervene on individual neurons, but the paper describes those indicators as unstable, context-dependent, and potentially disruptive to language ability. The authors investigate whether broader structural representations provide more dependable signals and whether components associated with detecting toxicity should be distinguished from those involved in generating it.

Experiments on Jigsaw and ToxiCN show that aggregated layer-level features are more robust than single-neuron signals. The authors also identify a conceptual problem in treating toxicity-detection components and toxicity-generation components as interchangeable. Their proposed method, EigenShift, uses an eigen-decomposition of the model's final output layer to selectively intervene on components aligned with generation.

The authors report precise toxicity suppression without impairing linguistic competence. EigenShift requires no additional training or fine-tuning, has minimal computational cost, and is supported by theoretical analysis. The contribution connects a more interpretable structural decomposition with targeted intervention: the relevant distinction is whether a component helps identify toxic content or participates in producing it.
neurips-2025-redefining-experts-interpre.tldr: EigenShift targets generation-aligned components of a language model's output layer to suppress toxicity without additional training.

paragraphs: High-resolution medical images create a difficult tradeoff for vision transformers. Small patches can preserve useful detail, but the resulting long token sequence makes computation and memory requirements grow quadratically. Symmetrical Hierarchical Forest addresses this by changing how image information is packaged into tokens and reconstructed from the transformer's outputs.

SHF adaptively patches an image to increase information density within tokens and encode hierarchical spatial structure in the input embeddings. A reverse depatching operation maps the output embeddings back, removing the need for convolution-based decoders. The authors describe SHF as compatible with any vision transformer without architectural changes, allowing the hierarchy to be handled through input and output processing.

On PAIP whole-slide images at 64K² resolution, the reported alternatives are 3–32× speedups or Dice-score increases of 2.95%–7.03% under the same computational budget relative to the compared production models. On BTCV and KiTS, training is six times faster, with accuracy gains of 6.93% and 5.9% against models without SHF. These results support adaptive tokenization for efficient high-resolution segmentation.
neurips-2025-shf-symmetrical-hierarchica.tldr: SHF adaptively packages image detail into hierarchical tokens, improving medical segmentation efficiency and reported accuracy without changing transformer architectures.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation trains a smaller student model using information from a larger teacher. Diverse teacher perspectives can improve the transfer, but maintaining several teachers adds computational cost. This paper creates multiple perspectives by attaching branches to one teacher, aiming to obtain useful diversity with a more economical source of supervision.

Two objectives shape the branch outputs through their angular relationships. One increases the angles between augmented views while keeping them close to the original teacher output. The other encourages an even arrangement of views around that output. The combined knowledge from the original teacher and these augmented views is then distilled into the student.

The theoretical analysis shows that the objectives increase ensemble diversity and reduce an upper bound on expected ensemble loss. Experiments show improvements over an existing knowledge-augmentation method across varied configurations. The approach also works with other distillation frameworks and produces consistent generalization gains in the reported evaluations. Its contribution is a controlled way to diversify supervision without requiring multiple separate teacher networks.
neurips-2025-single-teacher-view-augment.tldr: Multiple angularly diversified branches on one teacher improve knowledge distillation while avoiding the cost of separate teacher networks.

paragraphs: TCM-Ladder addresses a gap in evaluating language models for Traditional Chinese Medicine: existing datasets have limited coverage and focus mainly on text. The authors introduce a unified question-answering benchmark that includes images and videos alongside textual material, allowing evaluation across a wider range of tasks and subject areas.

The dataset contains more than 52,000 questions assembled through automated and manual filtering. It covers disciplines including foundational theory, diagnostics, herbal formulas, internal medicine, surgery, pharmacognosy, and pediatrics. Question formats include single-choice and multiple-choice items, fill-in-the-blank questions, diagnostic dialogue, and visual comprehension. This combination broadens both the knowledge being tested and the forms in which models must use it.

The authors train a reasoning model and conduct comparisons involving nine general-domain and five TCM-specific language models. They also propose Ladder-Score, which assesses terminology use and semantic expression in answers. The contribution is a shared multimodal evaluation resource and a domain-focused scoring method; the abstract does not report a winning model or numerical comparative results.
neurips-2025-tcm-ladder-a-benchmark-for-.tldr: TCM-Ladder provides over 52,000 multimodal questions and a domain-specific scoring method for evaluating Traditional Chinese Medicine language models.

paragraphs: Transfer attacks create adversarial examples using accessible surrogate models and attempt to carry those examples over to an unknown target. Ensemble-based methods use several surrogates and may query the target to refine the attack. This paper argues that earlier evaluations presented overly favorable settings, obscuring the influence of surrogate choice, target robustness, and query-based refinement.

TransferBench evaluates these factors through 17 settings on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. It includes different surrogate–target combinations, robust target models, and comparisons with methods that do not refine attacks through target queries. This design tests both whether attacks transfer under harder conditions and whether the additional query mechanism contributes useful improvements.

The evaluated methods fail to generalize well to the more challenging scenarios, and query-based refinement provides little or no benefit in the reported findings. Those results challenge prior claims of reliable, query-efficient transfer. The benchmark makes evaluation conditions central to understanding attack success and leaves dependable black-box transfer attacks as an open research challenge.
neurips-2025-transferbench-benchmarking-.tldr: TransferBench finds that evaluated ensemble transfer attacks struggle in harder settings and gain little or nothing from query-based refinement.

paragraphs: Diffusion policies learn robot actions from expert demonstrations, but their inference procedures often inherit choices developed for image and video generation. This paper argues that action distributions have different properties: they are structured and low-dimensional. Adapting denoising to those properties allows the evaluated policies to operate effectively with as few as five neural function evaluations.

The authors build on that observation with genetic denoising, a population-based sampling method. It selects denoising trajectories with low risk of going outside the learned distribution, aiming to improve both performance and stability. With this strategy, their method solves challenging tasks using only two neural function evaluations while matching or improving performance.

Evaluation covers 14 manipulation tasks from D4RL and Robomimic, with different action horizons and inference budgets. Across more than two million evaluations, the method consistently outperforms standard diffusion-based policies and achieves gains of up to 20% with fewer inference steps. The results support tailoring diffusion sampling to robot-action structure when seeking faster, effective control.
neurips-2025-two-steps-diffusion-policy-.tldr: Genetic denoising selects low-risk action trajectories, enabling two-evaluation diffusion policies with matching or improved manipulation performance.
